column1: # model-throughput, 2026-10-15: does a batch read by Falcon-OCR or PaddleOCR-VL finish sooner at concurrency 1 or 6, with two readers at once, or with the model kept loaded?
# Batch: 10 one-page PDFs cut by hybrid-run.sh (OCR-SAMPLE ids s02 s03 s04 s09 s10 other, s17 s40 s41 s42 s47 newspaper), through score-gate (OCRModel.start, the helper) with accurate mode on:

# each reader set for every kind (Falcon: align, regions on newspapers; Paddle: regions), memory setting 5 GB (the default), shipped runtime and Resources/read-model.py. Each leg ran alone under the heavy lock.

# Scratch helper only (not committed): Recogniser.modelReading with VISIONOCR_MT_SLOTS lock files (2 = two readers at once) and VISIONOCR_MT_STATS logging each call's times, footprint peak and read-model.py's JSON line.
# batch_wall_s: gate start to the last published PDF. reader_busy_s: sum of reader process lifetimes; reader_wait_sum_s: summed time helpers waited for the reader lock.

# mean_read_s: read-model.py's read_s (after load); mean_overhead_s: lifetime less read_s (interpreter start, imports, weight load, image preparation); mean_load_s: its load_s alone (page cache warm).

# overhead_share: overhead over reader busy time. max_reader_peak_mb: the guard's footprint peak of one call; max_two_peaks_mb: the largest sum over two overlapping calls. No page failed and the guard stopped none.
# min_free_mb and swap_end are vm_stat free+speculative and swap used: not a measure of headroom on macOS (file cache keeps free low; swap was 2.9 GB before the first leg).
